card.keepWhy: Half a faith, honestly brought, is enough to begin.
sources: Mark 9:14-15 (Jesus comes down to find the disciples arguing with scribes; the crowd runs to greet him)
Mark 9:17-18 (the father: his son has a spirit that throws him down; the disciples could not cast it out)
Mark 9:22-23 (“If you can do anything, have compassion on us, and help us.” Jesus: “If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes”), World English Bible, lightly modernized
Mark 9:26-27 (the boy lies as if dead; Jesus took him by the hand and raised him up, and he arose)
Matthew 28:17 (“When they saw him, they bowed down to him, but some doubted”)
check: Shot 1 says the boy “suffered terrible fits.” Mark describes a spirit that throws him down; the lesson leaves the cause unnamed to keep it gentle. Confirm this is acceptable.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? do you ever feel you’re supposed to be sure about God, and you’re just not?
options: then you’re in good company. this story has a father just like you.
that’s honest. hold onto it while you listen.
good. this one might help you sit with someone who isn’t.

steps.line: A father brought his son to Jesus’s friends. Since childhood, the boy had suffered terrible fits. The friends tried to help, and couldn’t.
steps.label: Mark 9:17-18

steps.line: Jesus came down from a mountain into the middle of an argument. The father stepped forward: “If you can do anything, take pity on us and help us.”
steps.label: Mark 9:22

steps.q: Jesus hears the words “if you can.” How do you guess he answers?
o: He asks his friends why they failed
He turns the words back: “If you can?”
He tells the father to come back when he’s sure
steps.why: He throws the father’s own words back to him, gently.

steps.line: “If you can?” said Jesus. “All things are possible for the one who believes.”
steps.label: Mark 9:23

steps.line: At once the father cried out, “I believe. Help my unbelief!”
steps.label: Mark 9:24

steps.q: The father says “I believe” and “help my unbelief” at the same time. Why doesn’t Jesus send him away?
o: He finally said the right words
Honest faith can hold doubt too
Jesus wanted the crowd to see
steps.why: He didn’t fake certainty. He brought what he had, and asked for help with the rest.

steps.line: Jesus spoke, and the boy grew still. Then Jesus took him by the hand and lifted him up, and he stood.
steps.label: Mark 9:26-27

steps.q: Even after Easter, Jesus’s eleven friends meet him on a mountain. What does Matthew say they did?
o: They asked to touch his wounds
They all fell down and worshiped
steps.why: Matthew 28:17, the last scene of his gospel. The friends sent out to the whole world still include doubters, and they’re sent anyway.

steps.line: Even his closest friends wrestled with doubt. After Easter, on a mountain, the gospel says, “they worshiped him, but some doubted.”
steps.label: Matthew 28:17

steps.q: Later, alone, the friends ask Jesus why they couldn’t help the boy. What does he tell them?
o: “This kind comes out only by prayer.”
steps.why: Mark 9:29. The friends had tried on their own. The father, half sure, did the one thing they hadn’t: he asked.

say: here’s what i love. the father’s prayer isn’t polished. it’s half sure and half scared, and jesus takes it.
christians have prayed his words for centuries. many teach that faith isn’t the absence of doubt. it’s trusting God with both.

steps.q: The father came with half a faith, and some of Jesus’s friends doubted. What does that suggest about how much faith you need to begin?
o: Enough to have no questions left
Enough to bring what you have
steps.why: Small and honest is enough to start. The father’s whole prayer was five words long.

today.say: if you’re carrying a doubt, don’t hide it. take the father’s five words, “i believe. help my unbelief,” and pray them, or just read them slowly tonight. watch, learn, or join in: your choice.
options: good. that prayer has carried a lot of people. it can carry you.
that’s okay. just keep the words. honesty is already a beginning.
